title: #7 Sean Walker, Sean Walker Racing Ford Sierra RS500, BTCC 1991
note: Placeholder only, no confidence in the livery. No photo, TV frame or BBC graphics drawing of Walker's car was found (he did not start at round 2, so the car is not in the grid graphics). Drawn as a plain white Sierra RS500 with the standard ESSO number board on the front door and the name on the rear side window; colours, sponsors and wheels are unknown. Lead to check: Motor Sport, May 1991, 'Under scrutiny: Trakstar' (https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/may-1991/28/under-scrutiny-trakstar) says Trakstar built three cars, one for customer Sean Walker, and that the car Gravett raced on 1 April was used by Walker on 14 April (Snetterton). If so, Walker's round 2 car was the Trakstar Sierra (Shell colours, Sapphire-based) and not an RS500; the entry lists and 1990sbtcc.com ('Looking Back at 1991, Part 1') still say RS500, so the drawing is unchanged. Logos (2026-11-16): none; no reference for the car's sponsors. 2026-11-16: the Trakstar lead was checked again and is not confirmed, so the drawing stays an RS500. Against it: Super Touring Register vehicle 283 (https://supertouringregister.com/register/vehicle/283/) lists the one Trakstar Sapphire with Gravett at both Silverstone (1 April) and Snetterton (14 April), and says the second shell was never finished, so Gravett cannot have moved to a new car at round 2 as Motor Sport planned; 1990sbtcc.com 'Looking Back at 1991, Part 1' (https://1990sbtcc.com/2021/04/01/looking-back-at-1991-part-1/) says Walker withdrew because 'the restricted RS500' was outclassed, which fits a restricted Group A turbo car, not the 2-litre Trakstar car; the Autosport round 2 and TCN entries and racingyears.com (https://racingyears.com/race/1991_British_Touring_Car_Snetterton) all list a Ford Sierra RS500. The Motor Sport May 1991 piece is a preview of the team's plan (three cars: Gravett, Mike Smith, customer Walker); Motor Sport June 1991 (https://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/june-1991/53/the-british-touring-car-championship/) only calls Walker a customer of the team. No photo of Walker's car found (Getty, STR, supertouring.co.uk and Peter Still 1991 galleries).
